questions.stem: A local exhaust hood is moved twice as far from a small contaminant source without changing airflow. What is the most likely result?

Capture velocity will remain unchanged at every distance from the hood
Capture will improve because a larger room volume is drawn toward the hood
Only duct friction changes; source capture is unaffected by hood distance

questions.stem: At a hood-performance troubleshooting visit, a supervisor proposes: "Capture will improve because a larger room volume is drawn toward the hood". The underlying case is: A local exhaust hood is moved twice as far from a small contaminant source without changing airflow. What is the most likely result? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Capture will improve because a larger room volume is drawn toward the hood
Capture velocity will remain unchanged at every distance from the hood
Capture effectiveness will decrease sharply, so the hood should be repositioned close to the source or airflow redesigned
Only duct friction changes; source capture is unaffected by hood distance
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Exterior hood capture velocity falls rapidly with distance. Placing the hood close to the source is generally more effective and energy efficient than relying on remote capture.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Capture will improve because a larger room volume is drawn toward the hood' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling source capture and hood placement principle.
The proposed response 'Capture velocity will remain unchanged at every distance from the hood' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling source capture and hood placement principle.
The proposed response 'Only duct friction changes; source capture is unaffected by hood distance' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling source capture and hood placement principle.

questions.stem: At a duct-system balance check, a supervisor proposes: "Place a pedestal fan behind the worker to disperse dust through the room". The underlying case is: A powder transfer can be partially enclosed without interfering with operation. Which ventilation design is generally preferred? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Use an open canopy hood above the worker for a heavy settling dust
Place a pedestal fan behind the worker to disperse dust through the room
Increase duct velocity while leaving the source fully open and distant from the hood
Use as much enclosure as practicable with inward airflow through controlled openings
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Enclosure reduces required airflow and prevents contaminant escape. Canopy and dilution approaches are usually weaker for source-generated dust where enclosure is feasible.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Use an open canopy hood above the worker for a heavy settling dust' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling enclosing hood design principle.
The proposed response 'Place a pedestal fan behind the worker to disperse dust through the room' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling enclosing hood design principle.
The proposed response 'Increase duct velocity while leaving the source fully open and distant from the hood' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling enclosing hood design principle.

questions.stem: At a contaminant-control retrofit, a supervisor proposes: "Reduce hood openings while keeping the same process emissions and no make-up air". The underlying case is: A new exhaust system removes substantial air from a tightly closed building. Doors become difficult to open and hood performance is unstable. What should be evaluated first? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Provide and balance conditioned make-up air so replacement air reaches the space without disrupting capture
Increase fan speed indefinitely without replacing exhausted air
Seal remaining building openings to increase negative pressure
Reduce hood openings while keeping the same process emissions and no make-up air
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Exhausted air must be replaced. Excessive negative pressure can reduce flow, interfere with doors and combustion equipment, and destabilize ventilation performance.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Increase fan speed indefinitely without replacing exhausted air' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling make-up air principle.
The proposed response 'Seal remaining building openings to increase negative pressure' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling make-up air principle.
The proposed response 'Reduce hood openings while keeping the same process emissions and no make-up air' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling make-up air principle.

questions.stem: At a make-up air assessment, a supervisor proposes: "Lower duct velocity so particles have more time to reach the collector". The underlying case is: Dust settles in horizontal ducts even though the hood captures material at the source. Which corrective action is most relevant? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Add room dilution fans while leaving deposited dust in the duct
Verify transport velocity, duct geometry, and balance, then correct the conditions allowing particulate deposition
Lower duct velocity so particles have more time to reach the collector
Close the branch damper serving the highest dust-loading process
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Particulate systems require sufficient transport velocity and suitable duct design to keep material suspended; reducing velocity or adding room mixing does not solve deposition.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Add room dilution fans while leaving deposited dust in the duct' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling duct transport velocity principle.
The proposed response 'Lower duct velocity so particles have more time to reach the collector' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling duct transport velocity principle.
The proposed response 'Close the branch damper serving the highest dust-loading process' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling duct transport velocity principle.

questions.stem: At a fan selection meeting, a supervisor proposes: "Remove all blast gates so no branch can ever be adjusted". The underlying case is: A branch hood has inadequate flow after another branch is opened. The fan is operating normally. Which diagnostic step is most useful? Judge performance solely by whether the fan motor sounds louder
Measure branch flows and static pressures to determine whether the system is unbalanced or losses differ from design
Assume the contaminant concentration changed and replace sampling media

questions.stem: At a confined-space purge estimate, a supervisor proposes: "Treat collector resistance as affecting removal efficiency but not the fan operating point or delivered airflow". The underlying case is: A fan is selected only by its free-air flow rating, but the installed system includes long ducts, elbows, and a collector. Why may actual airflow be inadequate? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Treat collector resistance as affecting removal efficiency but not the fan operating point or delivered airflow
Fan curves apply only to natural ventilation systems
Duct losses increase airflow above the free-air rating
The fan must operate against total system resistance, and its operating point is where the fan curve intersects the system curve
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Free-air ratings do not represent installed performance. The fan and system curves determine the actual flow at the required pressure.

The proposed response 'Fan curves apply only to natural ventilation systems' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling fan operating point principle.
The proposed response 'Duct losses increase airflow above the free-air rating' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling fan operating point principle.

questions.stem: At a ventilation commissioning test, a supervisor proposes: "Dilution ventilation is prohibited for every gas and vapor regardless of conditions". The underlying case is: A highly toxic contaminant is released unpredictably near workers, and the generation rate can vary rapidly. Why is general dilution ventilation a weak primary control? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: It may not prevent high local concentrations, and the uncertain generation rate makes reliable dilution difficult
Dilution ventilation is prohibited for every gas and vapor regardless of conditions
Dilution works only when contaminants are visible as dust
General ventilation always creates an oxygen-deficient atmosphere
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Dilution is best for relatively low-toxicity contaminants with predictable generation and good mixing. Highly toxic, variable, near-worker releases favor source capture or enclosure.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Dilution ventilation is prohibited for every gas and vapor regardless of conditions' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling dilution ventilation suitability principle.
The proposed response 'Dilution works only when contaminants are visible as dust' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling dilution ventilation suitability principle.
The proposed response 'General ventilation always creates an oxygen-deficient atmosphere' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling dilution ventilation suitability principle.
